the jumper. Like, it doesn't look
smooth, but that leg kick saves
everything. All of the sudden, it's
smooth as can be. And look at his other
foot while he's in the air. It like
turns diagonal and he lands on it like
that. I guess my point in sharing this
is when he's running around screens or
running in transition or just catching
and shooting, he doesn't have to be
perfectly positioned. And a lot of
shooters have to have everything
perfect, set on balance, same type of
footwork every time. But with Michael
Porter Jr., it feels like it's different
every single time. Besides that leg
kick, Brooklyn is moving him around more
often, whether it's off screens, in the
handoff situation, or him cutting, he
was standing in one spot more often in
Denver. So on NBA.com, you can filter
play type, and it turns out for
handoffs, cuts, offscreens, he's
averaging a total of 8.9 possessions per
game. For perspective, last season in
Denver, he was averaging 5.9 possessions
per game with those types of plays.

because he's pretty much the main factor
offensively. And I think this is
allowing him to get in a different type
of rhythm as a scorer. And also, he's
just naturally probably playing with
more confidence with all this newfound
freedom. Man, don't get it twisted. I I
believe he's still playing within the
flow offensively. And in terms of
offense, he's been a huge floor raiser.
With him on the floor, they have 118.7
offensive rating. That's good for top 10
in the league pace. Meanwhile, without
him, 106 offensive rating. Literally,
that would be the worst offense in the
league. That's how impactful of a scorer
and shot maker he's been. You can say,
"Oh, it's empty stats because he's in
Brooklyn and they only have whatever
five wins." But I feel like that's
really underelling what he's doing. I
mean, what the heck is this great close
out by Scotty Barnes? It's looking like
a lost possession and he just saves it
because of his insane shot making
ability. There's more variety to his
game. He's taken 9.7 two-pointers. His
previous careerhigh was 7.3.
He's averaging four shots in the
restricted area per game, shooting
84.2%.
He's getting to the foul line more
often, 4.6 free throws per game. His
previous careerhigh was 2.5. This
season, he's taking 1.2 driving layups
per game compared to6 last season. And
he's finishing 54.5%
of the time. As you can tell, he's way
more dynamic as a scorer. It's not just
three point or bust anymore for him.
It's also impressive with this newfound
responsibility. He's still maintaining
the same level of efficiency. He's
averaging 18.7 field goals attempted per
game. His previous careerhigh in Denver
was 13.6, yet he's still shooting 49.6%
from the field. My favorite moment from
him this season was when he just took
over in the fourth quarter against
Boston. Six-point game. He's running off
a screen. Pump fake. Get the defender in
the air and then he fades all the way
back to create separation and space for
the jumper. Nothing but net. Four-point
game now. Running off some screens. He
has a free driving lane. Goes right at
the rim protector. Pushes him back with
all that momentum and sneaks it in the
other side. Now they're up by six. He's
setting a screen and then he goes to the
dribble handoff and look at the fear in
the defender's eyes that he shook loose.
Unfortunately for them, they're just too
slow. They cannot stop him. Up by seven
points around the screen and look at
this sexy spin move right into the up
fake to get the defenders jumping. And
then he leans back to the open space and
floats it up and one. They're up by
eight points now. And think about it,
all quarter long he's been running off
screens up top. So the Celtics are
prepared. Well, guess what? Take this
back door slam jama. A double-digit lead
now. Look how physical they are off the
basketball. Finally, he shakes loose and
he shuts the door with this fadeaway
three. Actually, his toe was on the
line. Deep two-pointer. I digress. Icing
on the cake. He gets a free dunk. And to
celebrate, he's hanging on that rim
extra long. And I'm not going to lie, he
deserves it after that takeover. On top
of that, he's averaging a career-high
3.2 assists per game, and that's not
what he's known for. Clearly, Brooklyn
is getting the best possible version of
him. This is now three straight players,
Muel Bridges, Cam Johnson, and Michael
Porter Jr. Brooklyn's not winning games,
but I think their head coach deserves a
ton of credit for getting the most out
of these types. It'll be interesting to
see if Brooklyn keeps him or moves on
from him because I'm sure they can get
some nice assets in return with the way
he's playing. That's all I got though. I
want to hear your thoughts below in the
comments section. If you enjoyed,
remember to leave a like and subscribe.
Have yourself a great day and peace out.
